{{Short description|Polish physicist (born 1975)}}
'''Maciej Daniel Wojtkowski''' (born 1975) is a [[Polish people|Polish]] [[physicist]] and professor of physical sciences specialising in optics and biomedical imaging<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio">{{cite web |title=Maciej Wojtkowski: Bio-note |url=https://www.csz.pw.edu.pl/index.php/content/download/7280/53595/file/prof.M.%20Wojtkowski_Bio_eng_pl_2023.pdf |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=Center for Advanced Studies, Warsaw University of Technology |pages=1–2}}</ref>. He received the [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]] for developing Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography and introducing it into ophthalmic practice<ref name="Wojtkowski-FNP">{{cite web |title=Prof. Maciej Wojtkowski |url=https://fnp.org.pl/en/component/fnp_programs/program/nagroda-fnp/laureaci/3900 |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=Foundation for Polish Science}}</ref>. He is a co-founder of the International Centre for Translational Eye Research (ICTER) at the [[Institute of Physical Chemistry of the Polish Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="ICTER-institute">{{cite web |title=International Centre for Translational Eye Research |url=https://ichf.edu.pl/en/icter |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=Institute of Physical Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and the centre's director<ref name="Wojtkowski-ICTER">{{cite web |title=Maciej Wojtkowski, Prof. |url=https://icter.pl/people/maciej-wojtkowski/ |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=ICTER}}</ref>. 

==Education and career==
Wojtkowski graduated in physics from [[Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń]] in 1999. He received his [[doctorate]] in 2003 with the dissertation ''Spectral Optical Coherence Tomography Using Partially Coherent Light in Medical Applications'', and his [[habilitation]] in 2010 on the basis of ''Imaging Using Fourier-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography (FD-OCT)''<ref name="Glos-2015">{{cite journal |date=March 2015 |title=Nominacje profesorskie |trans-title=Professorial appointments |url=https://glos.umk.pl/panel/wp-content/uploads/GU_2015-03.pdf |journal=Głos Uczelni |language=pl |page=10}}</ref>. Both degrees were awarded at the university's Institute of Physics within the Faculty of Physics, Astronomy and Informatics<ref name="RP-2021">{{cite news |last=Kowalska |first=Karolina |date=19 October 2021 |title=Sztuczna inteligencja zbada chore oko |trans-title=Artificial intelligence will examine the diseased eye |url=https://www.rp.pl/zdrowie/art19027701-sztuczna-inteligencja-zbada-chore-oko |access-date=12 October 2026 |work=Rzeczpospolita |language=pl}}</ref>. He received the Polish academic title of [[professor]] of physical sciences in 2014<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />. His appointment document was presented at a ceremony at the Presidential Palace in Warsaw on 28 January 2015<ref name="Presidential-nomination-2015">{{cite web |date=28 January 2015 |title=Prezydent wręczył nominacje 53 profesorom |trans-title=The President presented appointments to 53 professors |url=https://www.prezydent.pl/kancelaria/archiwum/archiwum-bronislawa-komorowskiego/aktualnosci/nominacje/prezydent-wreczyl-nominacje-53-profesorom,19254 |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=Chancellery of the President of the Republic of Poland |language=pl}}</ref>.

He began working at Nicolaus Copernicus University in 1999 and led the Optical Biomedical Imaging Group within the Institute of Physics' Department of Biophysics and Medical Physics<ref name="Glos-2015" />. Between 1998 and 2001, he conducted research through an exchange programme at the [[University of Vienna]]. He worked at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 2003 to 2005 and also undertook research visits at the [[University of Kent]] in Canterbury and the [[University of Western Australia]] in Perth<ref name="Wojtkowski-FNP" />. He is affiliated with the Department of Biophotonics and Optical Engineering at Nicolaus Copernicus University<ref name="UMK-staff">{{cite web |title=Department of Biophotonics and Optical Engineering – people |url=https://www.ifiz.umk.pl/en/institute/department-and-labs/dboe/dboe-people/ |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń}}</ref>.

In 2016, following an international competition, he was selected to head the Department of Physical Chemistry of Biological Systems at the Institute of Physical Chemistry of the Polish Academy of Sciences<ref name="RP-2021" />. The department was established through the CREATE project ("The CREAtion of the Department of Physical Chemistry of Biological SysTEms"), funded under [[Horizon 2020]]<ref name="IPC-projects">{{cite web |title=Projects |url=https://ichf.edu.pl/en/projects |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=Institute of Physical Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences}}</ref>.

Together with [[Krzysztof Palczewski]], he founded ICTER within the institute<ref name="ICTER-institute" />. He has directed the centre since 2019.<ref name="RP-2021" /> He also heads its Physical Optics and Biophotonics research group<ref name="Wojtkowski-ICTER" />.

Wojtkowski leads the TRIO-VI CoE project, which supports ICTER's development into a [[Center of excellence|centre of excellence]] for [[translational research]] and innovation in [[ophthalmology]]<ref name="TRIO-ICTER">{{cite web |title=Horizon Europe WIDERA – Teaming for Excellence / EU |url=https://icter.pl/grants/teaming-for-excellence-widera-horizon-europe/ |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=ICTER}}</ref>. The project began in January 2025 and is scheduled to end in December 2030. It received €15 million in [[European Union]] funding through the Teaming for Excellence action under [[Horizon Europe]]. The Institute of Physical Chemistry coordinates the project, with [[University College London]] and the [[Vision Institute|Institut de la Vision]] associated with [[Sorbonne University]] as strategic partners. Its activities include research collaboration, training and the translation of research findings into ophthalmic practice<ref name="TRIO-CORDIS">{{cite web |title=Translational Research and Innovation in Ophthalmology Vision – Centre of Excellence |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101136570 |access-date=12 October 2026 |website=CORDIS |publisher=European Commission}}</ref>.

== Research ==
Wojtkowski studies the interaction of light with tissue and develops optical methods for imaging living organisms. His research includes [[optical coherence tomography]], [[fluorescence imaging]] of the retina and two-photon vision<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.

=== Optical coherence tomography ===
In 2002, Wojtkowski and his collaborators published results of ''in vivo'' imaging of the human retina using Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography<ref name="OCT-2002">{{cite journal |last1=Wojtkowski |first1=Maciej |last2=Leitgeb |first2=Rainer |last3=Kowalczyk |first3=Andrzej |last4=Bajraszewski |first4=Tomasz |last5=Fercher |first5=Adolf F. |year=2002 |title=In vivo human retinal imaging by Fourier domain optical coherence tomography |journal=Journal of Biomedical Optics |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=457–463 |doi=10.1117/1.1482379 |pmid=12175297}}</ref>. In 2003, with Tomasz Bajraszewski, Piotr Targowski and Andrzej Kowalczyk, he presented a high-speed spectral optical coherence tomography method that enabled real-time imaging of the eye. The exposure time for an individual axial scan was 64 microseconds<ref name="OCT-2003">{{cite journal |last1=Wojtkowski |first1=Maciej |last2=Bajraszewski |first2=Tomasz |last3=Targowski |first3=Piotr |last4=Kowalczyk |first4=Andrzej |year=2003 |title=Real-time in vivo imaging by high-speed spectral optical coherence tomography |journal=Optics Letters |volume=28 |issue=19 |pages=1745–1747 |doi=10.1364/OL.28.001745 |pmid=14514087}}</ref>.

Between 2003 and 2006, prototypes of his tomograph were tested at ophthalmic clinics in Boston, Pittsburgh and Bydgoszcz. In 2005, he began collaborating with Optopol on industrial production of the device<ref name="Wojtkowski-FNP" />.

=== Two-photon vision and retinal imaging ===
In 2014, Wojtkowski led research into two-photon vision that demonstrated the role of two-photon absorption in the isomerisation of retinal pigments producing visual sensations. In 2021, he and his collaborators presented ''in vivo'' images of the human retina obtained using two-photon-excited fluorescence<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.

His research group at ICTER develops imaging methods that use both the amplitude and phase of light, including techniques based on spatiotemporal optical coherence manipulation (STOC)<ref name="ICTER-institute" />.

=== Research projects ===
He received support through the [[Foundation for Polish Science]]'s START (2003), POWROTY/HOMING (2006) and TEAM (2011) programmes. In 2007, he received a European Young Investigator Award grant<ref name="Wojtkowski-FNP" />.

From 2017 to 2022, he led the "Two photon vision and two photon eye imaging" project (2x2-PhotonVis), funded through the Foundation for Polish Science's TEAM-TECH programme. It sought to develop methods and instrumentation for functional studies of vision using two-photon processes<ref name="IPC-projects" />.

From 2018 to 2021, he led the institute's participation in IMCUSTOMEYE ("IMaging-based CUSTOMised EYE diagnostics"), a Horizon 2020 project concerning the use of [[photonics]] and modelling in personalised ophthalmic diagnostics<ref name="IPC-projects" /><ref name="ICTER-report">{{cite web |title=ICTER's Overview Report 2019–2023 |url=https://icter.pl/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/ICTERs-Overview-Report-2019-2023-1.pdf |access-date=12 October 2026 |publisher=ICTER}}</ref>.

From 2019 to 2023, he led the "International Centre for Translational Eye Research" project (MAB/2019/12), funded through the Foundation for Polish Science's International Research Agendas programme, through which ICTER was established<ref name="IPC-projects" />.

== Awards and honours ==

* 2001 – scholarship from ''[[Polityka]]'' through its "Stay with us" programme<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.
* 2004 – Professor Stefan Pieńkowski Award<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.
* 2008 – Young Scientist Medal of [[Warsaw University of Technology]]<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.
* 2010 – Prime Minister's Award for his habilitation dissertation<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.
* 2012 – Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science in mathematical and physical sciences and engineering, for developing Fourier-domain optical coherence tomography and introducing it into ophthalmic practice<ref name="Wojtkowski-FNP" />.

== Memberships ==
Wojtkowski served on the Committee of Biocybernetics and Biomedical Engineering of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Glos-2015" />. He became a Fellow of the [[Optica (society)|Optical Society of America]] in 2015 and a corresponding member of the [[Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2016<ref name="Wojtkowski-bio" />.
